findings.how_to_check: Compare valGainTarget (28%) in replication/results/create_figures_SSHA2025.tex with valGainAncTarget (16.0%) and valGainFsTarget (11.5%) in replication/results/validation_fixed_initials.tex. In Stata on temp.dta, count records where linked_before==1 & linked_after==1 & id_A_before==id_A_after & validated_before!=validated_after; 165,580 identical kept links change validation status solely because mi1940 changed.
findings.suggested_fix: Retain one fixed 1940 middle initial across both link versions in CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do (such as Ancestry's mi1940_anc, as implemented in commit 8e8990d) and update the paper text at lines 98 and 548 to report the true fixed-initial gain (16.0% under Ancestry, 11.5% under FamilySearch). If the 28% moving-initial figure is kept, explicitly describe it as conflating link changes with middle-initial transcription changes and prominently report the decomposition into link composition vs initial re-reading.
findings.title: Reverting create_figures_SSHA2025.do to own-file middle initials conflates link quality with validator re-transcription and inflates the headline 28% gain
findings.what_the_code_does: CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do:73,83 reverts to own-file 1940 middle initials, computing validated_before = mi`beg_yr'==mi1940 using mi1940 from the Ancestry link file, and validated_after = mi`beg_yr'==mi1940 using mi1940 from the ML model link file. Lines 211-220 compute valGainTarget = 100*((sv_after/sv_before)-1) (= 27.8% -> 28%), which evaluates the percentage change when both the link partner and the 1940 validation standard change simultaneously.
findings.why_it_matters: The paper (DHTS-2026-10-12.tex:97-98, 548-549) claims a 28 percent increase in match quality (65% to 84%) on discordant records, interpreting this as evidence that newly recovered links are genuine rather than spurious. However, diagnostic validation_fixed_initials.do shows that holding the 1940 initial fixed reduces the target-group gain to 16.0% under Ancestry (valGainAncTarget) and 11.5% under FamilySearch (valGainFsTarget). For 829,471 kept links pairing the exact same individuals, validation jumps from 63.4% to 79.2% simply because mi1940 was re-transcribed. Reverting the code produces an inflated metric where more than half of the apparent 19.4 percentage-point gain is driven by re-reading initials rather than link quality.

findings.how_to_check: Run git --no-pager diff HEAD -- replication/claims.toml replication/claims_report.md. Run python replication/check_claims.py to verify that all claims report MATCH despite the known divergence between valGainTarget and valGainAncTarget.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the assertions in replication/claims.toml that tie headline validation gains to fixed-initial diagnostic outputs, or register explicit assertions for the decomposition components (ppLinks, ppReading) and require the draft to state them before marking claims as matching.
findings.title: Claims registry deletes assertions and explanatory notes that flagged the moving-validator discrepancy
findings.what_the_code_does: The working tree diff deletes assert = "abs(valGainTarget - valGainAncTarget) < 0.05" from claim intro-val-gain, and deletes assert = "abs(valGainTarget - valGainAncTarget) < 0.05" and assert = "abs(valGainAll - valGainAncAll) < 0.05" from claims results-validated and results-all in replication/claims.toml. It also deletes lines 80-91 of replication/diagnostics/validation_fixed_initials.do which asserted that temp.dta matched the fixed Ancestry validator. Consequently, replication/claims_report.md changes from 3 ASSERT FAILED to 50 MATCH.
findings.why_it_matters: The replication check check_claims.py now provides false assurance: it confirms only that the draft's text matches the output of the moving-validator script, while silencing the assertions that guarded against the divergence between the headline 28% and the fixed-initial diagnostics (16.0% and 11.5%). Deleting assertions turns a documented empirical defect into an unflagged clean run.

structured_output.summary: The uncommitted changes revert CODE/create_figures_SSHA2025.do to using moving 1940 middle initials, causing the headline 28 percent match-quality gain to conflate link improvement with re-transcription of the middle initials themselves. When evaluated against a fixed 1940 initial, the target-sample validation gain drops to 16.0 percent under Ancestry and 11.5 percent under FamilySearch. Concurrently, the working tree deletes the claims registry assertions in replication/claims.toml that caught this discrepancy, producing a false clean bill of health in claims_report.md. The single most important fix is to retain a fixed 1940 middle initial across both link versions and update the paper text to report the true fixed-validator gain.

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
